_readme: The Legends roster — twelve signature-style producers. Edit a number and the next render uses it; delete the file to regenerate the built-ins. Same schema as crew_config.json.
These follow the crew's instrument sound-variation rules only; their likeness rules (tight swing, home-weighted grammar, no evolution, 4/4) live in the engine.

Owner decision 2026-07-22: the "built" real-producer names stay, INTERNAL ONLY — no rename, no drop. They may only ever appear in the local batch-player UI (owner's own reference). Exported file names, stems, and titles must keep using the sound-alike codename (the dict key / preset["title"]), never preset["built"]. Re-decide before anything here ships publicly.

Farrow.listen: the live-band era, not the minimal one — that one is Glass Cat's: a real rock kit played by hand, kick and snare loose by 3 ms, a hi-hat and ride keeping time where a snap used to, guitars carrying the chords, funk-rock syncopation, sci-fi blips over the top, and still bone dry — no reverb, no dirt

signature._note: harmonic fingerprint (HARMONY-IDENTITY-PROPOSAL Addendum v2, 2026-07-23, wired 4th after No Alias/Swish Beatz/Razor all cleared audition). CORRECTION 2026-07-23: earlier notes in this file/proposal claimed the schema has an 'alt' field for a legend's second harmony mode -- checked the code, that's wrong. preset['alt'] is the drum-era alt-snare/reverb mechanism (see crew.py), unrelated to harmony. No engine mechanism exists for rolling between two full harmony modes per beat, and building one wasn't asked for, so this wires ONE mode only: research found Farrow genuinely bimodal (classic-minimal 2000-04 near-atonal vs later pop-era major/song-structured), and its own synthesis picked classic-minimal as the more identifiably 'Neptunes' sound -- that's what's here. The later major/pop mode is a documented, deliberately NOT-built follow-on, same honest-scope pattern as the Miami Bass/reggaeton rhythm-defined gap in the original proposal. Also flagged and left unsolved: Farrow and Swish Beatz (already wired) are both synth-dominant and will sound closer to each other than their real records do -- the distinguishing trait (pluck/bell timbre + huge negative space vs. horn-stab + density) has no field yet. Not yet audition-rendered. | BATCH 4/FINAL, 2026-07-24 (owner: finish up with the DJs). This closes the pre-07-23 legend backlog -- 12/12 legends now upgraded past their original loop/synth-only ceiling. RESOLVES the gap this file's own research flagged: 'Swizz and Farrow would eventually render near-identically on chord_source alone ... the real distinguishing trait (horn/brass-stab timbre + dense arrangement vs. Farrow's pluck/bell + huge negative space) has no field yet.' instrument_sampler now HAS that field. Web research confirms: 'funny little chimes', 'wide open spaces left up to the listener's imagination', built from as few as 4 sounds total (Grindin'). bell+pluck primary, one synth stab kept (their actual single lead synth), no horns -- that word is Swizz's now. | CHIP ADDED 2026-07-24 (owner request, 'video game sounds used with Pharaoh'). Checked before adding: N.E.R.D.'s 'Lapdance' (a Neptunes track) is documented as using synth lines 'reminiscent of rayguns or video game sound effects from the 8-bit era' -- so this is a real, specific trait of the source, not an unrelated bolt-on. Replaced the generic 'synth' slot (was [['bell', 3], ['pluck', 2], ['synth', 1]]) with 'chip' at the SAME weight (1 of 6) rather than adding a 4th option or raising the total -- his beats were already mostly bell/pluck with one occasional synth colour, and this keeps that ratio; chip just replaces what that occasional colour IS. No chip_tuning override: Neptunes are 'laser precision', not deliberately out of tune like New Math, so the default equal temperament stays. This is the chip voice's second use on the roster (after New Math/Chiptune) -- still the sanctioned exception, never a return to generic synthesis.

Farrow._research_note:
NEW-BUILD 2026-09-05, fourth legend through the pass (after Doc Day, Razor, Mustang). Backup: legends_config.pre-farrow-2026-09-05.json.

THE HEADLINE, and it is not a tuning fault: Farrow was a DUPLICATE of Glass Cat, one of the nine. Same 98 bpm, same five lanes (kick/snare/clap/snap/stamp, no hat), same kit tags word for word (kick clean/tight/pop, snare clean/rim/snap, snap snap/finger, stamp click/zap/glitch/laser), same 18 ms late clap, both built on 'The Neptunes / Pharrell'. Owner 2026-09-05: 'I have a version of him in the 9 I want to keep. I want this build to be a different era than that' — and, one message earlier, 'Nerd'. So Glass Cat keeps the Neptunes minimal era and Farrow becomes N.E.R.D.

That split is not a preference, it is documented, and in Pharrell's own reasoning. Wikipedia (In Search Of...): the 2001 album was 'largely electronic', drum machines and synths, 'a sound more typical of Pharrell Williams and Chad Hugo's production work as The Neptunes'; on 2002-03-12 they WITHDREW it and reissued the whole record re-recorded with live drums and guitars played by the power-pop band Spymob. Pharrell's stated reason: 'as N.E.R.D. was to be an entirely different venture to his and Hugo's work with the Neptunes, the band's music should also sound different, hence the decision to re-record the album.' Two DJs, two eras, and the artist himself says they are meant to be different records.

SOURCES
- Wikipedia, In Search Of... (N.E.R.D.): 2001 electronic version vs   2002-03-12 re-recorded 'rock version', live drums + guitars by Spymob,   'raw, live energy'; genres funk rock / rap rock. Pharrell's quoted reason   for re-recording, above.
- Chad Hugo to MTV News, 2003-12-08 (via Wikipedia, Fly or Die): 'We're the   ones playing the instruments live this time. I just started playing guitar   last year so I'm learning as we go. PHARRELL'S PLAYING DRUMS.' Questlove   and Lenny Kravitz play on 'Maybe'. So by album two the drums are a person,   not a machine.
- Sound On Sound, 'Recording The Neptunes' (Dan Daley, July 2005), engineer   Andrew Coleman on the N.E.R.D. tracks 'Rock Star' and 'Lap Dance': Pharrell   plays a standard drum kit, Coleman cuts 16 bars into a loop, 'that's where   a lot of the feel of their records comes from — it's not just machines and   loops.' This quote was the whole argument for loosening his timing, and it   is scoped to N.E.R.D., which is exactly this preset now.
- Uncut on Fly or Die: 'N*E*R*D can replicate machine hypersyncopation at   the drop of a hi-hat' — the syncopation survives the move to a live kit,   so the grammar was left busy rather than simplified.
- Gearspace, 'THOSE neptunes/pharell drums': 'The Neptunes were never DJ/  cratediggers... nearly all the sounds used on the earlier stuff (that   wasn't live band or live percussion) was presets from popular workstations'   — no crate dust in either era. Supports leaving dust/vinyl/wow at 0.

CHANGES
1. listen line rewritten to the N.E.R.D. era, and it names Glass Cat so the    next session cannot re-merge them. Owner's call, twice.
2. CLAP LANE DROPPED (kit, lanes and grammar.clap). Asked in plain language,    answered 'Give it to Glass Cat alone'. The ~18 ms late clap is the    documented NEPTUNES flam and was the single loudest reason these two    sounded alike. tests/test_crew.py:92 asserts that flam on GLASS CAT, not    on Farrow, so nothing breaks.
3. HAT LANE ADDED (kit + lanes + grammar). A rock kit has a hi-hat; the old    'a snap keeping time instead of hats' is a Neptunes-minimal trait and now    belongs to Glass Cat. Tags closed/tite/ride = 71 of 452 real files. `tite`    is in there because this library spells it that way — `tight` matches 1.
4. SNAP DEMOTED from timekeeper to colour: gain 0.4 -> 0.3, jitter 1 -> 2 ms,    modes offbeats/sparse/answer/eighths -> sparse 0.5 / answer 0.3 /    offbeats 0.2. Kept rather than deleted because live hand percussion is    documented for this camp.
5. TIMING LOOSENED: kick and snare jitter 1 -> 3 ms, hat 3 ms. Sourced to    Coleman and to Hugo's 'Pharrell's playing drums'. 3 ms is the same amount    the owner chose for Mustang on 2026-09-05; the AMOUNT is mine, the    direction is sourced. One line to move.
   NOT DONE: no lane was pushed or dragged (offset stays 0 everywhere). No    source says a N.E.R.D. drummer sits early or late, and inventing a    direction is how Otto Grit and Half Light get their identity — it is not    free decoration.
6. TASTE TAGS rewritten to words that exist in his filenames, then    own_soundbank ON. Order matters, same as Razor and Mustang. What was    there: kick pop=0 DEAD and tight=1 (the `tite` trap); snare snap=0 DEAD    and rim=23 which is the sidestick trap that cost a whole Dre round trip;    snap finger=8 of which SEVEN are 'finger cym tree' — finger CYMBALS, the    identical trap found on Mustang the same day; stamp click=0 and zap=0    DEAD. Now: kick dry/hard/gate = 33 files, all genuinely dry hard kicks,    no lofi, no `stomp` (a foley pack), no `brazillian funk`; snare    'hard dry'/'med dry'/'dry_snare'/'snr dry' = 14, deliberately the    multi-word forms because plain `dry` on snare also drags in    HWIP_Dry_SideStick, 'sn2 ss dry' (ss = sidestick), 'sn2 rim dry' and —    worst — 'sn4 flam dry', a snare that is ALREADY a flam; snap `snap` = 15    real snaps and zero chimes; stamp laser/drip/glitch = 12; hat = 71.
7. kick_flavors ALSO dropped its 10% 808 branch. Caught by reading the
   printed sample list on the first structure render: beat 2 came back
   with 'PLAYOFFS - 808 Thin.wav' as the kick under a listen line that
   says 'a real rock kit played by hand'. The TR-808/909 are documented
   for the 2001 ELECTRONIC In Search Of... (mathewgarland's Neptunes
   equipment list) — which is the era Glass Cat keeps, and the exact
   thing the 2002 re-record replaced with a live band. He is now one
   flavour, no 808.
   The old kick_flavors also carried the same dead words and OVERRIDES kit['kick'] on    every composed beat (pattern_gen.py:1326), so fixing the kit alone would    have changed nothing. The 808 flavour's wants were emptied — the 808 is a    must-word matched against the PATH, and the pool has no adjectives.
8. extras rebuilt. The fx 'blips' slot was zap/laser/glitch = 6 live of    three words; now laser/drip/glitch = 12. The perc slot was labelled    'woods' and asked for block/clave/tabla — block=1, clave=0, TABLA=10, so    his 'woods' colour was in practice a tabla pool, and tabla is    Timberline's signature instrument. Now cowbell/tamb/bongo = 68, labelled    'live perc', which is what the sources actually describe. A third slot    added: crash, because a rock kit has crash cymbals.
9. chord_source bell 3 / pluck 2 / chip 1 -> GUITAR 3 / bell 2 / chip 1.    The single most sourced change available: 'live drums and GUITARS'    (Wikipedia), Chad Hugo learned guitar for this record, Spymob is a guitar    band. Checked before wiring, the tag lesson applied to instruments:    instrument_sampler reports 112 playable guitar samples, and no legend was    using the voice. chip stays, and is now BETTER sourced than it was — the    raygun/8-bit note in his signature block cites 'Lapdance', which is an    N.E.R.D. track.

DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED
- allow_dirt STAYS OFF. Asked in plain language — funk rock, Trouser Press   calls the record 'filthy', and one weak source says the re-record used   'heavy distortion' — and he answered 'Stay completely clean'. Note the two   words do not actually fight: 'bone dry' in his line means no reverb, which   is a different knob from distortion, and he was told that before choosing.   dust/vinyl/wow are all 0 already and the sources agree (no crate digging in   either era), so unlike Razor there was no buried grime to switch on.
- `drive` 1.4 is left where it is and WILL NEVER PLAY while allow_dirt is   off — clean_renders strips the hot master drive. Recorded here rather than   silently zeroed, because a config that lies is exactly what hid Razor's   fault for months. If dirt is ever switched on for him, that 1.4 arrives   with it.
- No mix_eq of his own, so he gets the house EQ including +2 dB at 8 kHz.   Razor got that air CUT because an SP-1200 at 26.04 kHz physically could not   make it. The opposite is true here: workstation ROM samples and a live kit   through a modern desk have real top end. Leaving the default is the   researched answer, not an oversight.
- `glue` left at the roster default. Sound On Sound lists Pharrell's   favourite outboard (Tube-Tech CL1, dbx 160, LA-2A, Neve 9098, Summit) but   in the context of a NORMALLED VOCAL CHAIN — 'vocals are always on input   one'. Nothing in any source says what he does to a drum bus. Unsourced, so   untouched. Same discipline as Razor's glue.
- `sidechain` 0.15 — no source names it either way. Left, and named as   unsourced rather than dressed up.
- bpm stays 98. 'Lapdance' is around 92, 'She Wants to Move' around 100,   'Rock Star' around 104 — 98 sits in the middle and inside his signature's   own 95-115 range. Changing it would have been taste, not research.
- kick grammar weights and hit counts untouched. Uncut's 'machine   hypersyncopation' says the syncopation survives the live kit, so there was   nothing to fix.

LEFT INCONSISTENT ON PURPOSE, SAY IT OUT LOUD
- The rest of the `signature` block (key roots C/G/A, mode minor 3 / lydian 1   / mixolydian 1, the vamp progressions) was written for the classic-minimal   near-atonal era — that block's own note says so. Funk rock leans major and   mixolydian. Only chord_source was moved, because guitar is directly quoted   in a source; re-picking his modes and progressions is the harmony system's   own proposal, not this drum/sound pass, and doing it quietly here is the   blanket-apply the skill forbids. FLAGGED, not fixed.
- GLASS CAT STILL CARRIES THE SAME DEAD TAGS Farrow had (kick clean/tight/  pop, snare clean/rim/snap, snap snap/finger, stamp click/zap/glitch/laser)   and the open sound bank, so his picks are random from the whole bucket   today. He is one of the NINE and the owner said keep him — the nine are   explicitly out of scope for this pass. Not touched. Written down here so   it is a known state and not a discovery.
- Farrow's locked stamp was 'Cymatics - LIFE - Rain and Windchimes 4.wav' —   a field recording of rain, riding every beat he has ever made, because the   open sound bank wiped his click/zap/glitch/laser tags. Cleared from   ~/.reason_voice/crew_kits.json so lock_stamps re-picks against the fixed   tags. Third preset in a row where the producer tag was the wrong sound   entirely.

signature._note: DEEPENED 2026-07-24. Owner asked whether the FIRST FOUR legends (Doc Day, J Dillo, DJ Premium, Timberline) had been skimmed. Measured: their research notes averaged 583 chars vs 977 for the later eight, fewer progressions, fewer chord sources, and two of the four carried a modal key that silently returned ZERO in-key samples. Dre: dorian, not plain minor — the minor-tonic-to-MAJOR-IV move is the documented dorian tell and 'frequently used in funk'. gfunk_dorian_9 was added for the G-Funk GENRE on 2026-07-24 and proved there (owner: the reweight made it read sunnier); the same lesson applies to Dre, who is where that sound came from. piano added for the live-Rhodes half of his chain.

Doc Day._research_note: AUDIO/MIX PASS 2026-09-05, strictly research-based, new build (old kit/mix numbers were roster defaults, not researched -- discarded, not tweaked). Sources: his own quote in Studio Sound, Sept 2001, 'I like the compressors on the SSL. I usually have the ratio up to about eight or 10 on a lot of things' (Mastering The Mix, Decoding The Mix #4); mono-centric mix philosophy, checks translation on a single Auratone (same source); Focus... (Aftermath in-house producer) on SSL clarity/presence and 'hard-hitting drums' (Solid State Logic interview, 2026); Mike Elizondo brought in specifically for low-end/sub weight (Guitar World, Tape Op). high_db +2 @ 8kHz: 'crisp hard snare' (already in `listen`) -- direction is UP, opposite of Otto Grit's -1.5 (his research calls for dulled top end; Dre's calls for crisp). mid_db -1 @ 800Hz: separation -- sources agree elements are kept out of each other's way, not stacked/muddy. sub_layer 40Hz/0.15s/0.45: 'occasional deep sub' (already in `listen`) + Elizondo's low-end role + 'thick transients you feel in the chest' -- stronger than Otto's 0.35 because sub is a named part of THIS persona's identity, not incidental. allow_dirt left OFF (None) ON PURPOSE, not an oversight: no source anywhere calls for grit, dust, or vinyl noise -- every source says clean, crisp, surgical. This is the opposite direction from most of the roster and is the headline finding of this pass. kick_dist and mix_sat left at 0.0 ON PURPOSE: the SSL 'Asymmetric Drive' Focus describes is subtle preamp-stage harmonic coloring, not audible distortion/grit -- it is not the same thing kick_dist/mix_sat model for a persona like Rage Engine's wall-of-sound, so it was not force-fit onto those knobs. The 8-10:1 SSL compression ratio itself has no equivalent field on this schema (no per-persona compression-ratio knob exists) -- flagged, not guessed at. No personal twist (echo/chorus/phaser): that layer is nine-only per the 2026-09-03 house-EQ-and-twist decision ('the twist covers the nine only (not Legends, not genres)') -- not applicable here, and his own mono-compatibility obsession argues against a stereo-widening effect regardless. STATUS: measured against nothing yet -- NOT rendered, NOT heard. /Volumes/TBOTC 3 is not mounted from this session, so no audition batch could be built this round. Next step is an A/B/C batch (copy the shape of tools/make_otto_ab.py) once the drive is back. || GLUE COMPRESSION ADDED 2026-09-05 (second half of this pass): ratio 4.0, everything else (threshold -18 dB, 25 ms envelope, +2 dB makeup) inherited from OWNER_TASTE. This is the field the first half of the pass flagged as MISSING and refused to guess at -- it exists now: tools/crew.py passes a preset's `glue` block into groove.glue_compress, which already took these kwargs and was being called with none. DELIBERATELY NOT 8-10:1. His quote ('I usually have the ratio up to about eight or 10 on a lot of things', Studio Sound Sept 2001) describes SSL CHANNEL compressors on individual elements; this engine only has a single BUS glue compressor, so 8:1 here is a different effect from the one he described, and copying the number across would be the same force-fit this pass refused for kick_dist/mix_sat. 4.0 is 'harder than the roster's 1.8', which is the part the sources actually support -- read it as a direction, not as 'the Dre number'. Corroborated independently by the Gearspace thread 'Dr dre mixing techniques' (2016-09-03): 'clarity using heavy compression', 'hard SSL compression', 'sounds that only take up a certain part of the frequency spectrum and never fight with each other' -- that last one is the same separation argument behind mid_db -1 @ 800Hz. || mix_eq LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE, and worth knowing why: measured against groove.OWNER_TASTE['mix_eq'], only the low shelf actually moved (+1.0 @ 100Hz vs the roster's +1.5 @ 120Hz) -- mid and high are byte-identical to the roster default. groove.py's own note says only about a third of a low boost survives peak-normalise -> tanh -> master_to_lufs, so that band delivers roughly 0.2 dB. His mix_eq is very nearly a no-op and the sub layer is what will be heard. Not churned, because churning it would cost a re-render and buy nothing. || space ['gated', ['snare']] LEFT ALONE, FLAGGED NOT RESOLVED: it is a roster default shared by 7 of the 12 legends, never researched, and gated reverb is an 80s sound that sits oddly next to 'crisp hard snare' + 'clean, crisp, surgical'. Searched for a source either way on 2026-09-05 and found NOTHING that ties his snare to reverb or to dryness. Inconclusive, so it stays -- same handling as allow_dirt. Do not 'fix' this without a source. sidechain 0.2 and drive 1.45 are roster defaults too and are untouched for the same reason. || NEW BUILD 2026-09-05, second pass. Owner: 'I don't want any of the old rules to apply... I want this to be a completely new build so I can compare to what I have already versus what new research can create' -- 'for dr dre', i.e. SCOPED TO THIS PERSONA, not the engine. Rule for this pass: research replaces every field research actually speaks to; where the sources are silent the field is NAMED as silent rather than invented, because guessing is the thing he has forbidden outright. || space gated->dry: RESOLVED at last. It was never researched -- a roster default 7 of 12 legends share. The first pass left it because no source says 'dry' either. Under a new-build rule that reasoning inverts: gated reverb is an INHERITED default, and inheriting is what he ruled out. Everything sourced points away from it (clean, crisp, surgical, 'elements kept out of each other's way', 'sparse disciplined arrangement'), and gated reverb is an 80s drum effect no Dre source mentions. Dry is the research-neutral choice; gated was the inherited one. One line to revert. || sub_layer allow_peak_db 3.0 -- THE OLD RULE HE MEANT. crew's level cascade makes the kick the reference every other lane is scaled under (peak_ceiling_for returns None for backbone lanes), so kick_sub_reinforce was forbidden from letting the kick's peak grow. Measured consequence: the sub is INERT on any kick already at its peak, 4 of 6 real kicks, so 'occasional deep sub' and Mike Elizondo's whole documented role were doing nothing. That ceiling is a HOUSE rule, not a researched Dre trait, so it is lifted for him and him alone (default stays 0.0 for all 20 other presets). The cost is real and is not hidden: everything else in his beats sits further under the kick. || transient {gain 0.8, tau 3ms, kick+snare} -- groove.transient_shape has been written and tested since the engine was built and was wired to NOTHING. Same situation the glue knob was in. Sourced directly: Gearspace 'Dr dre mixing techniques' -- 'The smack on his drums; it sounds like a transient designer with hard SSL compression and good EQ'; Focus... (Solid State Logic interview) on 'hard-hitting drums'; his own listen line, 'heavy punchy kick, a crisp hard snare'. Applied to the raw lane before dirt/space/glue, where a transient designer actually sits. || STILL NOT INVENTED, named as silent: drive 1.45, sidechain 0.2. Both are roster defaults and both survive this pass ONLY because no source names either. The Gearspace post argues for clipping/saturation for perceived level, which would push drive UP, while every Aftermath source argues clean/surgical, which pushes it DOWN -- the sources contradict, so the number stays and is flagged rather than picked. Say the word and either becomes a rung in the next batch. KIT SELECTION, 2026-09-05 (second pass, after he heard the first batch): "It's not so much the kick. It's everything else." Root cause was not his numbers at all -- OWNER_TASTE['open_soundbank'] (house rule 2026-07-18) is read in one place, crew._pick_path, and it wipes `wants`/`must` BEFORE the pick tiers are built. Every researched taste tag on every preset in this repo is therefore dead code, and every kit pick is uniform-random from the whole role bucket. His audition got DECEPT_Sidestick and DECEPT_Lofi_Sidestick in the snare and perc lanes, HELLA HH MISC PERC 008 and Hats_OHs_162 (open hats) in the hat lane, and talking drum8 in a Dre beat. He chose the narrow fix: `own_soundbank` true for HIM ALONE -- one more inherited house rule dropped under the same 'no old rules for Dr Dre' call. The open bank still stands for the other twenty presets, by his decision and not by oversight. He also set the tie-breaker for this persona going forward: "Keep following the description as the top rule" -- the `listen` line above is the authority, which is why no snap lane was added (it names a crisp hard snare, not snaps) and why cowbell was added to perc (it names cowbell). SNARE LOCKED 2026-09-05: his listen line says the snare NEVER leaves 2 and 4, and he ruled a NEVER outranks the 2026-08-01 rule letting a legend take a groove seed's snare line ('Overrule old decisions when they cause problems'). snare_locked_24 is his alone; the other 11 legends still take the break's snare.

Kane East._research_note:
NEW BUILD 2026-09-05. Fourth legend rebuilt from research. Read this
before changing anything below; it says which numbers are sourced, which
are mine, and what nobody could answer.

The `listen` line below says "the industrial era" and not the album
title on purpose. That line SHIPS — it goes into .recipes/NN.json, the
sidecar that travels next to a beat — so the 2026-07-22 no-real-
attribution rule covers it exactly the way it covers `built`. The first
draft named the album and the executive producer and
test_recipe_never_carries_the_real_producer_name caught it. Everything
under a `_` key, this note included, is stripped recursively and may
name whoever it needs to.

WHY THE ERA MOVED (the reason this build exists)
Kane East was a duplicate. Sunday Chop, one of the nine crew DJs, is
also built = "Kanye West", and the two listen lines were nearly the same
sentence:
  Sunday Chop  "gospel bounce at 57% swing, driving pushed kicks, a BIG
               clap with a snare tucked underneath, tambourine offbeats;
               clean (MPC3000 = 16-bit)"
  Kane East    "chipmunk-soul era: driving pushed kicks, a BIG clap with
               the snare tucked underneath, 57% gospel bounce, tambourine
               offbeats, warm light dust and a vinyl bed"
Same bpm family, same swing, same clap/snare relationship, same perc.
Nobody had noticed because the twelve legends and the nine are audited
separately — the same fault that had made Farrow a copy of Glass Cat the
same day. Owner, asked directly: "kanye also has different eras and I
might have a version of him in the nine. If I do, give me an era that is
not the same." He then chose Yeezus over 808s & Heartbreak and Dark
Fantasy. Sunday Chop keeps chipmunk soul and was NOT touched — the nine
are out of scope for legend work and he has said so twice.

WHAT THE SOURCES ACTUALLY SAY
- "an abrasive, electronic soundscape with distorted drum machines and
  synthesizers ... industrial, acid house, electro, punk, Chicago drill,
  and horrorcore" — Wikipedia, Yeezus. This is the single sentence the
  whole build hangs on: DISTORTED DRUM MACHINES, not sampled soul.
- "West's orders to Rubin were to take the music in a 'stripped-down
  minimal direction', often removing elements already recorded"; West on
  Rubin, to Zane Lowe, Sept 2013: "he's not a producer, he's a reducer".
  Rubin cut it from 16 songs to 10 — Wikipedia, Yeezus.
- "built on alien, angular beats, slowly morphing drones and sirens,
  abrupt periods of silence" — Ted Scheinman, Slant Magazine, quoted in
  the same article. The siren and the silences are sourced, not invented.
- "an extravagantly abrasive album full of grinding electro, pummeling
  minimalist hip-hop ... industrial gear-grind" — Rolling Stone, same.
- Greg Kot, Chicago Tribune: "hostile, abrasive and intentionally
  off-putting", combining 1980s Chicago acid house, 2013 Chicago drill,
  1990s industrial and the avant-rap of Death Grips.
- The first sessions were in the living room of a Paris loft, and "West
  kept compositions simple in order to hear the tracks more clearly; too
  much bass or complexity would simply overpower the room's poor
  acoustics." He also "set parameters regarding sound and style,
  insisting that there be no 'bass wobbles'". Both Wikipedia, Yeezus.
  That is a documented reason for a short, tight kick and no sub.
- Thomas Bangalter (Daft Punk, produced four tracks) called the process
  "very raw" — same article.

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY
1. bpm 90 -> 130. Sourced as a direction only (acid house / industrial /
   the Black Skinhead pulse); the exact number is MINE. It also lands in
   a gap on the roster — Glass Cat 98, Chrome Dial 100, Night Metro 140.
2. Swing 57 -> 50 and jitter 2 -> 0 on kick/clap/snare. 57% gospel
   bounce is Sunday Chop's, by his own line. Machine time is what
   "distorted drum machines" and 1980s acid house mean. Hats, toms and
   the siren keep 1 ms so the top of the kit is not literally identical
   every bar.
3. Clap 0.9 / snare 0.5 -> both 0.8. "A BIG clap with the snare tucked
   underneath" is Sunday Chop's signature phrase. Here they stack into
   one hard machine hit. The amounts are MINE.
4. Perc lane: tambourine and shaker -> toms (drtom/drhtom/drbtom/rack,
   84 real tom samples), gain 0.3 -> 0.55. Tribal toms are the hook on
   this record; tambourine offbeats are the other era's. Sourced as
   direction; the gain is MINE.
5. allow_dirt: true, kick_dist 0 -> 6.0, mix_sat 0 -> 3.0. Direction is
   sourced hard ("distorted drum machines", "industrial gear-grind",
   "very raw"). THE AMOUNTS ARE MINE. Without allow_dirt the
   2026-07-18 clean-render rule strips every one of them, which is the
   same fault that had kept Razor's grime silent for months. Narrow
   opt-out, one preset, same shape as Otto Grit / Crate Prophet / Razor.
6. dust 0.35 -> 0.0 and vinyl -44 -> -80 (off). His old line promised
   "warm light dust and a vinyl bed" and — because he had no allow_dirt
   — it had never once played. Rather than finally switch on a soul-era
   vinyl bed under an industrial record, both are off and the line no
   longer claims them. This is the one place where turning a dead
   setting ON would have been the wrong fix.
7. space: gated -> dry. Gated reverb is an inherited roster default that
   7 of 12 legends share and an 80s effect no Yeezus source mentions;
   reverb also fills exactly the "abrupt periods of silence" the record
   is built on. Same reasoning that resolved Doc Day's and Farrow's.
8. Taste tags rewritten to words that exist in the filenames, then
   own_soundbank: true — in that order, because with the bank on and bad
   tags he would have been gated to whatever the dead words hit. What
   was dead before: kick "warm" 0 files, clap "big" 0, stamp "vocal" 0
   and "soul" 0. And "boom" on the kick matched 3 files of which 2 were
   808s, the exact trap that cost Doc Day a round trip.
9. kick_flavors rewritten and the 30% "808" branch dropped. It overrides
   kit["kick"] on every composed beat (pattern_gen.py:1326), so fixing
   the kit alone would have changed nothing. 808s are Hitt Kid's line,
   and West's own documented parameter for this record was against heavy
   bass in that room.
10. library: soul/motown/boom-bap/funk -> electro/house/punk/drill/
    minimal/techno, p 0.5 -> 0.35. The five genre words are Wikipedia's;
    the weights and p are MINE.
11. His producer tag was a FIELD RECORDING OF A RIVER — the lock in
    ~/.reason_voice/crew_kits.json was "Cymatics - LIFE - River - Light
    4.wav", riding every beat he had ever made, because the open bank
    wiped his tags and lock_stamps picked at random from 356 fx files.
    Fourth wrong producer tag in four legends. Lock cleared so it
    re-picks from siren/alarm — 7 files. It was first written as
    siren/alarm/riser/white-noise (20 files) and the lock landed on a
    white-noise sweep; narrowed because 'sirens' is the word the source
    actually uses and a riser is not a producer tag.

LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE
- drive 1.4 and sidechain 0.2: no source names either. They stay at
  what they were rather than being invented upward.
- mix_eq: REMOVED, so he renders through the ear-approved house EQ. The
  one genuinely sourced EQ number I found belongs to the OTHER era and
  therefore to Sunday Chop, not here: Craig Bauer, who mixed Late
  Registration, in Sound On Sound Feb 2006, on West asking for the drums
  to "knock" more — "I assumed it meant more low frequencies, but he
  said no ... I heard that and said OK, that's low-mids, around 800Hz to
  1kHz." The house EQ CUTS 1 dB at exactly 800 Hz. That is worth knowing
  for Sunday Chop one day; it is not this record.
- glue: left at the roster default. Doc Day got 4.0 because his sources
  demanded hard compression. No Yeezus source says anything about bus
  compression, so copying that number across would be the blanket-apply
  the new-build process forbids.
- key roots Bb/F/G: no source names a key. Unchanged.
- No invariants. There are no absolute words in the new listen line, so
  there is nothing to build a choke point for.

WHAT NOBODY COULD ANSWER
- No engineer interview for Yeezus itself surfaced with per-drum
  settings, the way Bauer's does for Late Registration. Everything about
  the amount of distortion here is a direction from critics and a number
  from me.
- The record's real tempos are all over the place (On Sight ~119, Black
  Skinhead ~130, I Am a God ~86/172). 130 is one choice, not the
  average.
- Craig Bauer's "not an ounce of reverb" quote is Late Registration, not
  this album, so it is NOT the reason space went dry here. The reason is
  the documented silences. Named so nobody later cites it wrong.

Swish Beatz._research_note:
NEW BUILD 2026-09-06, eighth legend through the pass.
Backup: legends_config.pre-swish-beatz-2026-09-06.json.

STEP 1b, CHECKED FIRST: Swizz Beatz is NOT in the nine (Dilla, Premier,
Pete Rock/Madlib, Timbaland, Pharrell, Kanye, Metro, Lex Luger, plus
three no-ones). No duplicate, no era question for the owner.

SOURCES — all his own words, Complex, "Swizz Beatz Tells All: The Stories
Behind His Classic Records (Part 1)", Insanul Ahmed, 2011-08-20.
- THE IDENTITY SENTENCE: "I was breaking down a lot of sonic doors for
  producers because when I came in it was the sample era. I was one of
  the first people to lead the synth era. It was keyboard — no sampling,
  just expressing your art through bugged out sounds."
- GEAR, and he is emphatic about it: "I was using the Trinities, these
  silver keyboards. The Triton hadn't come out yet"; earlier the Korg M1
  ("I did 'Money, Cash, Hoes' on the Korg M1 too"), a Dr. Rhythm, an old
  TR-808, an MPC60. On the Casio myth: "I've never seen a Casio that had
  THOSE TYPES OF HORNS or that could make the type of shit I was making."
  The horns are named by him, as the thing that identifies his records.
- THE ARRANGEMENT RULE: "I had this pattern where we would follow the
  beat and follow the lyrics with the melodies. So you would hear the
  beat playing the song."  The melody is locked to the drum rhythm — it
  does not float over it.
- THE SHOUTS ARE STRUCTURAL, not decoration: DMX's "What!" ad-libs "came
  about in the middle of us hyping him up. We left it in the track to add
  energy." And the "One, two, meet me outside" outro on "Party Up", which
  he was paid $15,000 extra to put on other people's records.
- WHY IT IS BLUNT: "Being a DJ was my biggest secret weapon. I was
  thinking about how people would react in the club. I knew how to
  control the crowd so I knew how to make records for the crowd."

CHANGES
1. THE INVARIANT — `zero_subtlety`. His listen line ends "zero subtlety
   and proud of it", and tools/legend_newbuild.py flags `zero` as an
   ABSOLUTE. Per the hard-rule-invariant skill that is a refusal, not a
   weight: the two backbeat modes that read as restraint, `sparse` (one
   hit where two belong) and `displaced` (the 4 nudged off the grid), are
   removed from his clap roll outright. They were 35% of it, and his
   snare copies his clap, so 35% of both. Choke point:
   pattern_gen.compose(), one branch, keyed on "gcells" in the spec.
   HIS HATS ARE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. The same line asks for "sparse
   shouting hats" — sparse is his identity up there and restraint down
   here. This is exactly the Doc Day trap in reverse: do not blanket-
   apply. Test: test_swish_beatz_refuses_the_subtle_backbeat_modes,
   proved red by removing the flag.
2. TASTE TAGS rewritten to words that exist in real filenames, THEN
   own_soundbank on — that order, as with every legend since Razor.
   What was dead:
     kick   knock=0, punch=1   -> hard=17 + stomp=29 + dry=22
     clap   big=0              -> clap=75 (the whole 76-file pool)
     snare  crack=0            -> hard=16 (see the `dry` warning below)
     stamp  horn=0, shout=0, vocal=0, siren=5 -> siren=5 + stab=11
   `stomp` is the direct hit: his line's first image is "big simple kick
   stomps" and the library holds 29 files with stomp in the name that not
   one of his old tags could reach. `dry` everywhere is sourced by
   elimination — his dust/vinyl/wow are all 0.0 already and nothing in
   the interview describes grime; he is a keyboard-and-drum-machine
   producer, not a crate digger, and says so.
3. THE STAMP, and this is the one that was quietly broken. His line
   promises "siren and horn color" and 3 of his 4 stamp tags matched
   NOTHING: horn=0, shout=0, vocal=0. Only siren survived, 5 files. Now
   siren + stab = 16. Named out loud, and CORRECTED 2026-09-06 after the
   owner asked the right question ("should you look for brass instead?").
   The first version of this note said the library has no horn samples at
   all. THAT IS FALSE and would have misled the next session. The true
   statement is narrower and is about WHICH POOL:
     * The DRUM ONE-SHOT buckets have no horns — horn=0 and brass=0
       across all 356 fx files and across every other one-shot bucket.
       The only hits anywhere are one melodic LOOP ("74 bpm_fm_mannequin_
       horn choir") and one "orch hit" in fx. So THE STAMP LANE cannot
       deliver his horns, which is the claim that actually matters here.
     * The MELODIC INSTRUMENT INDEX is a different pool entirely and holds
       38 REAL BRASS SAMPLES — Brass Fanfare, Horn Scream, Muted Horns,
       Brass Chop, Cresc Brass — spanning notes 43-84, 22 distinct
       pitches. Verified with instrument_sampler.covers(): brass covers a
       real triad in every register tried, and nearest() on middle C
       returns "60_Drown_Horns Cm.aif".
   His `chord_source` is [["horns", 3], ["synth", 2]] and "horns" is a
   REAL voice name — instrument_sampler.VOICES maps horns -> ("brass",).
   His horns already play, from the chord side, exactly as intended, and
   the interview vindicates that twice over: "those types of horns" is his
   own phrase for what identifies his records, and "no sampling, just...
   bugged out sounds" off a Trinity/M1 is exactly a synth horn stack.
   Do not re-add "horn" to the STAMP tags — that pool really is empty.
   Do not conclude from this note that he has no horns; he has 38.
   METHOD NOTE, because it cost a wrong claim: chord_source voice names
   are checked against instrument_sampler.VOICES, NOT against GROUP_NAMES.
   Checking the wrong list makes "horns", "strings", "loop" and "chip"
   all look dead when every one of them is real and handled.
4. The stamp is now re-picked PER BEAT (the 2026-09-06 roster change,

   "siren and horn color" describes.
5. kick_flavors: the 808 branch DROPPED, one flavor left. It OVERRIDES
   kit["kick"] on every composed beat (pattern_gen.py:1326), so fixing
   the kit alone would have changed nothing. DESCRIPTION-LED: his line's
   first image is "big simple kick stomps" and his era is 1998-2003 Ruff
   Ryders, not trap. He does name owning an old TR-808 in the interview,

THE 808 BRANCH IS GONE, AND THE REASON IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A TASTE
CALL. It was first cut to 0.15, then removed outright when the printed
sample list kept showing 808s. Measured over 300 composed beats: a
